channels.name: SATURDAY MORNING
channels.description: Wake up, pour the cereal, watch cartoons. Actual Saturday morning broadcast recordings, commercials and all.

channels.name: PRIMETIME
channels.description: Primetime exactly as it aired — sitcoms, dramas, and variety blocks taped straight off the network feed. Laugh tracks, station IDs, and 8pm commercials intact. The couch, the cathode glow, the show everybody watched.

channels.name: SYNDICATE
channels.description: The truth is out there, and it's on cable at 1 a.m. with the commercials still in. Off-air tapes of the shows that ran forever in syndication — Mulder and Scully, Quantum Leap, Stargate, everyone lost in space. Trust no one; tape everything.

channels.name: LATE NITE LOCAL
channels.description: It's 2 AM on public access. Someone is doing... something. You can't look away.

channels.name: HAPPY TREES
channels.description: Every episode of The Joy of Painting with Bob Ross — 31 seasons of happy little trees, almighty mountains, and quiet streams. The most soothing 26 minutes on television, now running 24/7.

channels.name: COMPUTER CHRONICLES
channels.description: Every episode of the PBS show that documented personal computing from 1983–2002. From the Apple II to the dot-com bust.

channels.name: OPEN MIC
channels.description: Spelunkr's community access channel. Local bands. Talent shows. The best show you'll never see twice.

channels.name: LIBRARY CARD
channels.description: The shows that sent you to the library: Reading Rainbow, Mister Rogers, Arthur, Wishbone and the Magic School Bus, all day.

channels.name: NATURE PRESERVE
channels.description: Longform nature documentaries from the golden age. Jungles, oceans, tundras, savannahs. Patient cameras and calm voices explaining a planet that was doing just fine before we got involved.

channels.name: UNPAID PROGRAMMING
channels.description: Infomercials, all night: the knives, the abs, the get-rich tapes, and a man who is very excited about a mop.

channels.name: RADIO-ACTIVE TV
channels.description: Music videos, VJ countdowns, and Headbangers Ball — someone taped over their sister's copy of Titanic with 6 hours of MTV.

channels.name: LATCHKEY-TV
channels.description: You let yourself in with the key around your neck and watched cable cartoons until your parents got home. VHS recordings of after-school cable tv toons, commercials and all.

channels.name: KERSPLAT
channels.description: Kids' game shows, back to back: obstacle courses, temple runs, the Aggro Crag, and a bucket of something green at the end.

channels.name: FINAL FRONTIER
channels.description: Space: the final frontier, on basic cable at 2 a.m. Every flavor of Star Trek beamed straight off the antenna — five-year missions, the next generation, the far side of the wormhole. Set phasers to rerun.

channels.name: ROCKET PUNCH
channels.description: Giant robots, one episode at a time: mecha anime from the super robots of the seventies to the real robots of the eighties.

channels.name: OVATV
channels.description: Anime from the back of the rental store: OVAs and films two at a time, long runs of one series, and Saturday Anime taped off the air.

channels.name: TOONERTIA
channels.description: Action anime on an unstoppable loop. Toonami recordings straight off the VHS, commercials and all.

channels.name: LATE NITE SWIMCLUB
channels.description: It's past midnight. The cartoons got weird. You should be asleep but you can't stop watching.

channels.name: HOMEROOM
channels.description: The guidance films they showed you on the classroom projector in 1955. How to be popular. How to go on a date. How to be a good citizen.

channels.name: MANDATORY VIEWING
channels.description: This video is required for all new associates. There will be a quiz.

channels.name: FALLOUT SHELTER
channels.description: The government's cheerful instructions for surviving the apocalypse, 24/7, 365 (or until the inevitable global thermo-nuclear war that destroys us all).

channels.name: DUSTY TRAILS
channels.description: This is where the pavement ends and the real work begins. We don't trade in noise or neon. Just dust, distance, and the kind of quiet that makes a man think twice about what he's saying.

channels.name: GUMSHOE
channels.description: Rain on the window, a client with a problem, and a detective who should have said no. Crime pictures, all night.

channels.name: IT CAME FROM
channels.description: It came from the drive-in. It came from the bottom of the lake. It came from a budget of $400. Horror flicks of a wide variety of quality levels. Scary.

channels.name: DAILY DREAD
channels.description: Pure horror. No sci-fi, no monsters from space — just the films that kept you up at night. Every night.

channels.name: GRAVEYARD SHIFT
channels.description: A horror movie is better when someone in a wig is making fun of it. The late-night hosts, movie and wisecracks intact.

channels.name: RAY GUN
channels.description: Ray guns, rocket sparks, and a cliffhanger every reel. The black-and-white serials that swore we'd have jetpacks by now — Flash Gordon, Buck Rogers, and every square-jawed spaceman who saved the Earth by Chapter 12. To be continued... forever.

channels.name: SIGNPOST
channels.description: There's a signpost up ahead. Twenty-six minutes of the uncanny, a narrator who already knows how it ends, and a twist you'll spot a half-second too late. Twilight Zone, Outer Limits, One Step Beyond — the anthology hour where the dial goes strange and stays that way.

channels.name: RUBBER HOSE
channels.description: Noodle arms, pie-cut eyes and a piano that plays itself. Cartoons from before anyone told them about bones, seven minutes at a time.

channels.name: MEDDLING KIDS
channels.description: A talking dog, four teens and a man in a rubber mask who would've gotten away with it. The whole Hanna-Barbera shelf, all day and all night.

channels.name: SUPLEX
channels.description: Wrestling the way it aired: whole shows, local promos, ads for hotlines and CDs, and a folding chair for every occasion.

channels.name: VACATION SLIDES
channels.description: Strangers' family vacation footage from the 1930s–70s. Silent 8mm film of places you've never been with people you'll never meet, set to period-accurate tunes. Vibe on, time traveler.

channels.name: OOPS ALL BUMPS
channels.description: Dev/test channel — nothing but bumps. Short placeholder videos trigger bump breaks every few seconds.

channels.name: TEST PATTERN
channels.description: Dev/test channel — eight short clips with a bump break every couple of minutes. For checking publishes, version switches and cycle wraps without waiting out a six-hour tape. Only visible with ?debug.
